question: Which of the following has invented the musical instrument Bamhum and Tikzik?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Moa Subong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Moa Subong** is a renowned musician from Nagaland, India.
 
• He is a member of the famous folk-fusion band **Abiogenesis**.
 
• Moa Subong is credited with the invention of two unique musical instruments, namely the **Bamhum** and **Tikzik**.
 
• The Bamhum is a bamboo-based wind instrument, while the Tikzik is a percussion instrument, both contributing to the innovative sound of Abiogenesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abiogenesis**

 
 
• Abiogenesis is a folk-fusion band from Nagaland, India, known for blending traditional Naga folk music with modern musical styles.
 
• The band was formed in 2005 and has gained recognition for their unique sound and musical innovation.
 
• Abiogenesis has performed at various national and international platforms, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of Nagaland.
 
• The band's music often features traditional Naga instruments along with modern instruments, creating a distinct fusion genre.
 
 
 
• **Bamhum**
 
 
• The Bamhum is a wind instrument made from bamboo, invented by Moa Subong.
 
• It produces a unique sound that is integral to the music of Abiogenesis.
 
• The Bamhum has been recognized for its innovation and contribution to folk music.
 
• It is played by blowing into it and using finger holes to create different notes and melodies.
 
 
 
• **Tikzik**
 
 
• The Tikzik is a percussion instrument also invented by Moa Subong.
 
• It adds rhythmic elements to the music of Abiogenesis, complementing the melodies of the Bamhum.
 
• The Tikzik is played by striking it with hands or sticks, producing a range of percussive sounds.
 
• It is crafted using traditional techniques and materials, reflecting the cultural heritage of Nagaland.
